# RESULTS -- humanist paragraphing sweep

Generated by `tally.py`. Every number below is computed from `judgments/*.json` joined to `KEY.json`; re-run `python tally.py` to reproduce.

**Unit of analysis:** the individual judge call. 576 calls over 282 distinct items.

## 0. Data integrity

- Items in KEY: **288**
- Judgment files: **24**, calls: **576** (a complete two-pass sweep would be 576)
- Batches never judged: **4** -- P1 ['P1-B12'], P2 ['P2-B03', 'P2-B10', 'P2-B12']
- Batches judged twice: **4** -- P1 ['P1-B01'], P2 ['P2-B01', 'P2-B05', 'P2-B11']
- Distinct items seen: pass 1 **264/288**, pass 2 **216/288**, either **282/288**, both **198**
- Items never judged at all: **6**
- Files whose self-reported `batch_id` does not match the batch they actually judged: **0** (none)

The 4 unjudged batches and 4 doubly-judged batches are the same defect seen from both ends: a dispatch off-by-one. It cost **0 of 576 planned calls** (0.0%) and it is not random with respect to content -- a whole batch is a seeded random draw, so the loss is unbiased across arm/treatment in expectation but does thin specific cells.

### Word-identity re-verification (independent of make_variants.py)

- Item files compared to their source passages after whitespace normalization: **288 checked, 288 identical, 0 differing**
- Source passages, each carrying all four treatments: **72** (four-per-passage: yes)
- Assertion in `make_variants.py` (`normalize_ws(treatment) == normalize_ws(source)`): **HOLDS, re-verified here**

This matters for section 3: the four paragraphing treatments are word-identical by construction, so any detection difference between them is attributable to paragraph shape alone. That is a genuinely clean comparison -- no confound from wording, length, topic, or register, because every treatment is the same text.

### 7.3 Verbatim examples, true-tell clusters

**tricolon-and-triads** (329 cites, 144 items) -- rule of three, stacked triads, announced enumerations that arrive at exactly three

- [gate-clean / essay / chunk / conf 3] A second triad in the middle: "I went for shorter books, skipped the slow middles, and steered around anything hard enough to stall me for a month"
- [raw-ai / review / as-authored / conf 4] Escalating triad: "badly designed doors everywhere, and then badly designed light switches, and then badly designed stovetops"
- [gate-clean / email / punchy / conf 4] Announced list counts: "Three findings surprised us" delivering exactly three; then "One caveat on all of this"
- [raw-ai / email / irregular / conf 4] Announced enumeration filled with perfect parallelism: "Three things. First... Second... Third..."

**uniform-beat-rate** (256 cites, 128 items) -- every paragraph or section lands the same number of rhetorical beats; metronomic cadence; sections built to identical shape

- [raw-ai / marketing / irregular / conf 5] Four bolded verb bullets ("**Receive.** **Put away.** **Pick.** **Count.**") of machine-uniform length and grammatical shape
- [raw-ai / essay / punchy / conf 4] "That framing concedes the argument before it starts" — essay-machine pivot into the counterargument beat
- [raw-ai / email / irregular / conf 4] Both incidents narrated in identical shape — cause, blast radius, exact duration ("40-minute partial outage", "22 minutes to diagnose and about 4 minutes to fix"), then a we've-since-added remediation
- [humanized / email / as-authored / conf 3] Reassurance beat: "Most weeks the secondary will never hear from PagerDuty at all"

**typography-and-punctuation** (230 cites, 119 items) -- em dashes, curly quotes, unicode decoration, and other punctuation regularities the gate treats as formatting law

- [gate-clean / essay / chunk / conf 3] Not one book, author, or title is named, in a piece entirely about a book spreadsheet — all specificity is numeric scaffolding (forty-one, fifty, three years, out of five)
- [raw-ai / essay / punchy / conf 4] "That framing concedes the argument before it starts" — essay-machine pivot into the counterargument beat
- [raw-ai / review / as-authored / conf 4] Em-dash-bracketed core-insight sentence: "Its core insight — that good design makes the right action obvious and the wrong action difficult — applies just as well to an API as it does to a stovetop"
- [gate-clean / email / punchy / conf 4] Statistics precise, humans anonymous — 200/143/61/28/40 branches, $500,000 and $2 million thresholds, "about 70 percent of the time", but not one named librarian or town

**announced-thesis** (198 cites, 106 items) -- essayistic hinge that states its own thesis; signposted structure; 'what this is really about'

- [raw-ai / marketing / irregular / conf 5] Chiasmus as thesis: "Instead of asking your team to adapt to the software, the software adapts to your team"
- [gate-clean / essay / chunk / conf 3] Aphoristic thesis dropped in as summary: "Reading isn't a productivity metric, and treating it like one turned a pleasure into a chore"
- [raw-ai / essay / punchy / conf 4] Closing tallies the anecdote back into the thesis with tidy arithmetic: "Two wrong cartridges, eleven days of dripping, and about forty dollars in shipping taught me what four minutes of expertise is actually worth"
- [gate-clean / email / punchy / conf 4] Antithesis as the hinge of the findings: "The most common complaint was not noise. It was the difficulty of enforcing expectations in a space that no longer signals its purpose architecturally"

**negative-parallelism** (185 cites, 100 items) -- not-X-but-Y in any form: inline, sentence-split, negated appositive, 'the job was never A, the job was B', 'X rather than Y' in a definitional slot

- [raw-ai / marketing / irregular / conf 5] Three stacked negative parallelisms: "Each step takes seconds, not minutes"; "Deployment takes a week, not a quarter"; "no hardware to purchase, no server to provision, and no consultant to hire"
- [raw-ai / essay / punchy / conf 4] Four consecutive antitheses carry the argument: "The practical task was never 'deliver a cartridge to my door.' The practical task was 'identify which cartridge I need.'"; "What I needed was not inventory. It was diagnosis."; "The inventory gets liquidated and redistributed. The knowledge does no...
- [gate-clean / email / punchy / conf 4] Antithesis as the hinge of the findings: "The most common complaint was not noise. It was the difficulty of enforcing expectations in a space that no longer signals its purpose architecturally"
- [raw-ai / email / irregular / conf 4] "rather than" antithesis is the recurring explanatory move: "held back deliberately rather than accidentally"; "caught by monitoring rather than by customers"; "writing the migration tooling before migrating anything, rather than migrating a few services by hand and then generalizing"

**aphoristic-closer** (158 cites, 94 items) -- epigram / aphorism / sententious line used to end a paragraph or the piece

- [gate-clean / essay / chunk / conf 3] Aphoristic thesis dropped in as summary: "Reading isn't a productivity metric, and treating it like one turned a pleasure into a chore"
- [gate-clean / email / punchy / conf 4] Reframing aphorism right after the data: "So the trend is not a retreat from quiet. Branches are packing quiet into smaller rooms with clearer walls"
- [humanized / email / as-authored / conf 3] Benefit restated as aphorism instead of instruction: "Two weeks means you hand off a system you have actually had time to learn"
- [gate-clean / marketing / punchy / conf 5] Stock aphorisms: "the wiki is where documentation goes to die", "None of that survives contact with a real company", "Documentation should make your team faster"

**performed-hedging** (137 cites, 84 items) -- hedges and caveats that read as inserted rather than felt; calibrated uncertainty as a stylistic tic; 'I can't prove that'

- [gate-clean / email / punchy / conf 4] Announced list counts: "Three findings surprised us" delivering exactly three; then "One caveat on all of this"
- [raw-ai / essay / irregular / conf 4] The steelman/self-caveat beat announced in advance: "I want to be careful here, because there is a version of this argument that is dishonest"
- [raw-ai / marketing / irregular / conf 5] Unattributed, hedged-quantitative proof: 'Customers report inventory accuracy climbing from the low nineties into the high nineties' - no customer named, no baseline, no method
- [raw-ai / review / as-authored / conf 4] Hedge-word tic in an evaluative claim: 'The vocabulary alone is arguably worth the price of admission'

**too-complete-no-friction** (121 cites, 61 items) -- the idealised path only: no dead ends, no digression, no troubleshooting, no unresolved thread, no failure modes

- [gate-clean / essay / chunk / conf 3] Every sentence advances the argument; no digression, no aside, no dead end
- [gate-clean / howto / as-authored / conf 3] Troubleshooting section containing exactly two problems, each stated as symptom-then-cause-then-fix
- [gate-clean / email / punchy / conf 4] Statistics that are individually vivid and jointly frictionless: '143 had reduced their designated quiet space since 2010', 'budgets above $2 million included one about 70 percent of the time', '61 branches had added a new quiet room... and 28 of those had also cut quiet space elsewhere'
- [gate-clean / essay / irregular / conf 3] Perfectly closed arc in under 200 words — spreadsheet, number, disappointment, deletion, moral — with no digression, no second incident, and no unresolved thread.

**listicle-in-prose** (108 cites, 71 items) -- an enumerated list wearing paragraph clothes; announced counts that resolve into exactly N items

- [gate-clean / email / punchy / conf 4] Announced list counts: "Three findings surprised us" delivering exactly three; then "One caveat on all of this"
- [raw-ai / email / irregular / conf 4] Announced enumeration filled with perfect parallelism: "Three things. First... Second... Third..."
- [gate-clean / review / irregular / conf 3] Announced count: "Two real drawbacks." delivering exactly two
- [gate-clean / howto / as-authored / conf 3] Troubleshooting section containing exactly two problems, each stated as symptom-then-cause-then-fix

**contraction-register-uniformity** (100 cites, 64 items) -- zero contractions in a register that should have them, or a contraction rate that never varies; register held perfectly flat

- [raw-ai / essay / punchy / conf 4] Zero contractions across the whole piece ("It did not fit", "I do not have and cannot easily describe", "it is not written down anywhere")
- [gate-clean / review / irregular / conf 3] Zero contractions in a casual first-person product note: "It is a plastic cylinder", "it just does not feel like", "I would buy it again", "It is also close to impossible to get wrong"
- [gate-clean / howto / as-authored / conf 3] Zero contractions throughout ("you do not need to install anything else", "Activation did not take effect", "you opened a new terminal tab and did not re-activate there")
- [humanized / essay / irregular / conf 4] The same four antitheses survive a looser, contraction-heavy rewrite: "the job was never 'deliver a cartridge to my door.' The job was 'work out which cartridge I need.'"; "I didn't need inventory. I needed a diagnosis"; "The stock gets liquidated and redistributed. The knowledge doesn't."

**closing-formula** (78 cites, 51 items) -- the summary close, the recap tricolon, the upbeat CTA, 'highly recommended'

- [gate-clean / marketing / punchy / conf 5] Triadic CTA close: "Start a free trial, invite the people who answer the most questions, and see how many of those questions stop coming"
- [raw-ai / review / as-authored / conf 4] Labeled verdict with a tidy prescription and no first-person reading experience anywhere in the piece: 'Verdict: highly recommended for anyone who builds things that other people have to use'
- [gate-clean / marketing / punchy / conf 5] Imperative triple as CTA: 'Import your SKU list, print your labels, and start scanning.'
- [raw-ai / email / chunk / conf 4] Limitations paragraph placed immediately after the findings and before the CTA: 'It's worth noting that our sample skews toward...'

**ai-vocabulary** (71 cites, 33 items) -- the flagged lexicon: delve, crucial, leverage, robust, seamless, tapestry, utilize, showcase, foster, elevate

- [raw-ai / marketing / irregular / conf 5] Vocabulary flags: "seamlessly", "robust API", "intelligently batched", "Seamless Integration With Your Existing Stack", "fundamentally different approach"
- [raw-ai / review / as-authored / conf 4] Reviewer boilerplate with no observation behind it: "is a testament to how well the framework has held up", "arguably worth the price of admission", "remains essential reading"
- [raw-ai / essay / irregular / conf 4] Names its own rhetorical moves as it makes them: 'That is the crucial asymmetry'; 'This is the part I want to argue with'; 'I want to be careful here, because there is a version of this argument that is dishonest'
- [raw-ai / essay / as-authored / conf 3] Meta-signposting sentences that name the essay's own moves: 'That is the crucial asymmetry', 'This is the part I want to argue with', 'I want to be careful here, because there is a version of this argument that is dishonest.'

**unattributed-proof** (51 cites, 34 items) -- anonymous customers, unnamed experts, generic institutions, evidence with no checkable denominator

- [raw-ai / essay / punchy / conf 4] Vague attribution framing: "We tend to talk about small shops as though...", "something that gets lost in conversations about retail"
- [gate-clean / email / punchy / conf 4] Too-perfect quote with vague attribution: "A branch manager in Ohio said it best: 'When the room had a door and a sign, people policed themselves. Now it's an open corner and I'm the sign.'"
- [gate-clean / marketing / punchy / conf 5] Unattributed metrics and anonymous customers: "lose something close to a day a week", "onboarding time... drops by about a third", "A 200-person fintech", "A hardware company"
- [raw-ai / marketing / irregular / conf 5] Unattributed, hedged-quantitative proof: 'Customers report inventory accuracy climbing from the low nineties into the high nineties' - no customer named, no baseline, no method

**concessive-then-correct** (49 cites, 29 items) -- concede the sentimental or naive framing, then correct it; 'sure, but'; 'I'd be lying if I said'

- [raw-ai / essay / punchy / conf 4] "That framing concedes the argument before it starts" — essay-machine pivot into the counterargument beat
- [humanized / essay / irregular / conf 4] A concession inserted to preempt the obvious objection: "Sentiment is in there somewhere, and I'd be lying if I said the drawer labeled in handwriting had nothing to do with it"
- [gate-clean / review / chunk / conf 4] Concession-shaped detail that reads as scripted balance: "produces a spatial effect I found interesting for two days and then never opened again"; "which got old fast, and you can turn it off"
- [gate-clean / review / chunk / conf 3] Each section grants exactly one reservation, with the concession arriving in the same position every time: 'Build quality is good, not exceptional'; 'Detail is good without being class leading'; 'Speech is reduced rather than removed'

**planted-detail-callback** (39 cites, 30 items) -- a detail planted early and recalled verbatim at the close; ring composition; no loose ends

- [raw-ai / essay / irregular / conf 4] Ring-composition callback constructed for the final line: the bench outside the bank 'replaced by a planter' returns as 'There is a planter there now, with the same shrub in it that they put outside the bank'
- [raw-ai / social / punchy / conf 5] Engagement-bait closer plus emoji bookends: thread-emoji in tweet 1 and 'What's worked for your team? 👇' at the end.
- [gate-clean / essay / as-authored / conf 4] Motif planted and then recalled exactly once: 'a drawer labeled in handwriting' in paragraph two, 'the drawer labeled in handwriting' in the final paragraph.
- [raw-ai / essay / punchy / conf 4] Airtight ring composition -- the bank bench 'replaced by a planter' in paragraph five returns as the closing image, 'a planter there now, with the same shrub in it that they put outside the bank'

**numbers-as-texture** (39 cites, 30 items) -- concrete numbers deployed at an unnaturally even rate as authenticity props; specificity theater; vague-precise quantities

- [gate-clean / email / chunk / conf 4] Calibrated-humility inserts that read as authenticity theater: 'The other half we cannot account for cleanly, so treat that number as directional' and 'I'm not confident the September version was any better.'
- [humanized / email / punchy / conf 4] Section headers fused into the preceding paragraph text: '## Where the migration landed As of September 26, 41 of 47 services run...' and '...treat that number as directional. ## What changes in Q4'.
- [gate-clean / social / irregular / conf 3] Nearly every numbered post lands on an engineered aphorism: 'That stung enough to act on.', 'Nobody has told me they went too high.', 'go look at it.'
- [gate-clean / email / as-authored / conf 3] Bolted-on epistemic caveat that reads as inserted rather than felt: 'The other half we cannot account for cleanly, so treat that number as directional.'

**anaphora** (38 cites, 25 items) -- three or more consecutive sentences or paragraphs opening the same way

- [raw-ai / essay / irregular / conf 4] Anaphora block enumerating beneficiaries: "Anyone in the third trimester... Anyone recovering from surgery, chemotherapy, or a broken foot. Anyone carrying groceries. Anyone with a heart condition, a lung condition, chronic fatigue, or a bad knee"
- [raw-ai / review / as-authored / conf 4] Escalating tricolon built by anaphora: 'you begin noticing badly designed doors everywhere, and then badly designed light switches, and then badly designed stovetops'
- [gate-clean / marketing / punchy / conf 5] Anaphoric negative triple: 'There is no hardware to buy, no server to provision, and no consultant to hire.'
- [gate-clean / marketing / chunk / conf 5] Anaphoric negative triple in the CTA section: 'no hardware to buy, no server to provision, and no consultant to hire.'

**balanced-clause-symmetry** (38 cites, 25 items) -- chiasmus, antimetabole, mirrored clauses, the balanced explanatory gloss

- [raw-ai / marketing / irregular / conf 5] Chiasmus as thesis: "Instead of asking your team to adapt to the software, the software adapts to your team"
- [humanized / email / as-authored / conf 3] Constructed antimetabole doing the justification work: 'the weekly handoff cost you more in context-switching than the shift itself cost you in pages' - the verb 'cost you' repeated against two different objects
- [raw-ai / essay / irregular / conf 4] Two mirrored three-adjective lists forming a single balanced antithesis - the strongest structural tell in the piece: 'The costs of having benches are visible, local, and attributable... The costs of not having benches are invisible, diffuse, and borne by people who are not in the room.'
- [gate-clean / marketing / punchy / conf 5] Chiasmus as the product thesis: 'The software adapts to your team instead of asking your team to adapt to it.'

**feature-benefit-marketing** (21 cites, 19 items) -- the feature-then-benefit compression, the positioning line, the value-prop sentence built to be quoted

- [gate-clean / marketing / punchy / conf 5] Zero contractions across ~750 words of consumer-facing marketing copy: 'It is in a Slack thread', 'cannot be searched', 'If the page does not exist yet', 'which have not been opened in a year'
- [humanized / marketing / irregular / conf 4] Chiastic positioning line: 'The software adapts to your team instead of asking your team to adapt to it.'
- [gate-clean / email / as-authored / conf 3] Manufactured pull-quote framed by 'A branch manager in Ohio said it best' with an unnaturally balanced payoff: 'Now it's an open corner and I'm the sign.'
- [raw-ai / marketing / as-authored / conf 5] Chiasmus as the positioning line: 'Instead of asking your team to adapt to the software, the software adapts to your team.'

**fragment-paragraph-beats** (14 cites, 13 items) -- one-thought standalone fragment paragraphs used for manufactured emphasis

- [gate-clean / review / punchy / conf 4] Arbitrary single-sentence paragraphing that cuts inside a single move: 'That is what the book actually does.' stands alone, then 'It retrains your attention instead of handing you conclusions' begins a new block.
- [humanized / howto / punchy / conf 4] Announced trio rendered as three orphan sentence-paragraphs instead of a list: 'You need three things before you start.' then 'A server running Ubuntu 22.04...', 'A registered domain name...', 'Ports 80 and 443 open...'
- [gate-clean / marketing / punchy / conf 4] Feature bullets de-listed into consecutive one-sentence paragraphs: 'Import your logo and colors once...', 'Clients pay by card or bank transfer straight from the invoice.', 'Expenses sort themselves into categories, which makes tax season shorter.'
- [humanized / marketing / punchy / conf 4] Isolated one-sentence paragraphs used for rhythm: 'Each step takes seconds.' / 'Palletline works the other way around.'

**teacherly-overexplaining** (5 cites, 5 items) -- hand-holding, explaining the obvious, 'let's break this down', reader instruction

- [raw-ai / howto / as-authored / conf 5] Explicit hand-holding transition: 'Let's walk through the process step by step.'
- [raw-ai / social / irregular / conf 5] Explicit thread-bait scaffolding: 'Let's break down exactly what happened. 🧵' opening and 'Found this useful? Follow for more on SaaS pricing and growth. 🚀' closing.
- [raw-ai / email / chunk / conf 3] Over-explained causal chain: 'This came directly out of the feedback from January's retrospective, where several of you noted that the weekly handoff was creating significant context-switching overhead.' — a real manager writes 'a few of you flagged this in the January retro'.
- [raw-ai / social / as-authored / conf 5] Engagement-bait bookends: 'Let's break down exactly what happened. 🧵' opening and 'Found this useful? Follow for more on SaaS pricing and growth. 🚀' closing

**stakes-inflation** (2 cites, 2 items) -- grand abstraction, world-historical framing, the sweeping unearned claim

- [raw-ai / howto / as-authored / conf 4] Grandiose value framing in sentence one: 'one of the most valuable skills a developer can pick up'
- [gate-clean / essay / chunk / conf 3] Unsourced sweeping claims stated as fact: "Cities have spent thirty years pulling them out anyway.", "Most cities cannot tell you how many public benches they own"

**thematic-tidiness** (1 cites, 1 items) -- one governing metaphor or theme carried cleanly through with no drift; the piece is about exactly one thing

- [humanized / essay / as-authored / conf 3] Anecdote engineered so every detail later pays off thematically — the handwriting-labeled drawer is planted in paragraph two and cashed in the final paragraph

### 7.4 Verbatim examples, false-tell clusters

### 7.5 Unclustered residue, samples

True-tell pool (951 strings unclustered):

- Stock scene-setting opener with triadic consequences: "In today's fast-moving supply chain, a single misplaced pallet can cascade into missed shipments, unhappy customers, and costly write-offs"
- Anonymized results with no attribution: "Customers report inventory accuracy climbing from the low nineties into the high nineties", "One regional distributor", "Another eliminated more than 400 hours"
- Triadic close: "I read slower, I quit more books, and I remember much more of what I read"
- Concreteness generated to order: "Kessler Hardware, which has been on the same corner since 1961", "changed its stem diameter in the mid-nineties", "a drawer labeled in handwriting"
- Stock review frame: "one of those books that changes how you look at the world"; "remains a foundational text for designers, engineers, and product managers alike"
- Obligatory-balance paragraph announced outright: "There are other weaknesses worth mentioning", then reversed by "Despite these limitations"
- Terminal "Verdict:" label plus a reading-order rider ("treat the first six chapters as the heart of the book")
- Abstract nominalization: "no longer signals its purpose architecturally"
- Four bolded section headers, each a balanced phrase: "**Where we landed on the migration**", "**What broke, and what we did about it**", "**What's changing in Q4**", "**What we need from you**"
- Evaluative tails welded onto facts: "which is a reasonable request and one we're happy to accommodate"; "which is the outcome we want even though neither should have happened"
- Balanced comparative doing the justification: "the weekly handoff cost you more in context-switching than the shift itself cost you in pages"
- One picturesque detail placed exactly at the close, on another rather-than frame: "I'd rather move a shift now than discover the clash at 3am on a Saturday"
- Bolded parallel headers structuring an email into a report: **Where we landed** / **What broke** / **Numbers** / **What's changing** / **What we need from you**
- Bullet metrics each formed as figure-plus-attribution: "Median deploy time dropped from 14 minutes to 6 minutes. The improvement is almost entirely from parallelizing the test stage."
- Trailing evaluative clauses: "which is a reasonable request and one we're happy to accommodate", "which is honestly better than I expected given the migration"
